hook.line: Tomás wants to tell Mariana how he feels about the café, and he notices two ways of saying it: the thing surprises him, or he is the one who gets surprised. Spanish keeps them apart.
hook.es: Me sorprende lo rápido que aprende.
hook.en: It surprises me how fast she learns.

examples.es: Me sorprende lo rápido que aprende.
examples.en: It surprises me how fast she learns.

examples.es: Me sorprendí de que la estación estuviera vacía.
examples.en: I was surprised that the station was empty.

examples.es: Me entristece ver el parque tan abandonado.

I felt sad when I remembered it.

rule:
There are two ways to say how something affects you.

1. The thing is the subject: *me sorprende*, *me entristece*, *me avergüenza*. It describes what causes the feeling. The verb agrees with the thing: *me sorprende su paciencia*, *me sorprenden sus preguntas*. After it come a noun, *lo* + adjective, an infinitive, or *que* + subjunctive.

2. You are the subject: *me sorprendo*, *me entristezco*, *me avergüenzo*, usually with *de* or *al*. It describes your own reaction, often at one moment: *me sorprendí de que…*, *me entristecí al…*.

English uses "it surprises me" and "I was surprised". Spanish keeps the two apart.
smallPrint: Teachers call the first group verbs of affect, like *gustar*, and the second the reflexive (pronominal) forms.

readAndPick.es: Me sorprende lo rápido que aprende.
options: It surprises me how fast she learns.
I surprise myself by how fast she learns.
She is surprised at how fast I learn.

readAndPick.es: Me sorprendí de que la estación estuviera vacía.
options: It surprises me that the station is empty.
I was surprised that the station was empty.
The station surprised everyone by being empty.

readAndPick.es: Me entristece ver el parque tan abandonado.
options: I got sad when I saw the park.
I cheered up the abandoned park.
It saddens me to see the park so neglected.
I felt sad when I remembered it.
It saddens me to remember it.
You felt sad when you remembered it.

readAndPick.es: Me avergüenzo de lo que dije.
options: What you said embarrasses me.
I'm ashamed of what I said.
He's ashamed of what I said.

readAndPick.es: Me avergüenza lo que dijo mi hermano.
options: I'm ashamed of what I said to my brother.
My brother is ashamed of what I said.
What my brother said embarrasses me.
Her questions surprise me.
Her question surprises me.
I'm surprised by my questions.

readAndPick.es: Me sorprendo cuando oigo esa canción.
options: That song surprises me.
I get surprised when I hear that song.
You get surprised when you hear that song.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *sorprende* or *sorprendo*: Me ___ lo rápido que aprende. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Me sorprende lo rápido que aprende.
yourTurn.why: The speed is the cause, so the thing is the subject: *sorprende*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *sorprende* or *sorprenden*: Me ___ sus preguntas. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: *Sus preguntas* is plural, so the verb is *sorprenden*.

yourTurn.prompt: It saddens me to see the park so neglected.
yourTurn.answer: Me entristece ver el parque tan abandonado.
yourTurn.why: The thing causes the feeling, so *me entristece* + an infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: I felt sad when I remembered it.
yourTurn.why: You are the one who reacted, so the reflexive form + *al*.

yourTurn.prompt: I was surprised that the station was empty.
yourTurn.answer: Me sorprendí de que la estación estuviera vacía.
yourTurn.why: Your own reaction, so *me sorprendí de que* + subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: What my brother said embarrasses me.
yourTurn.answer: Me avergüenza lo que dijo mi hermano.
yourTurn.why: The thing causes it: *me avergüenza* + what was said.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it your own reaction: Me avergüenza lo que dije.
yourTurn.answer: Me avergüenzo de lo que dije.
yourTurn.why: When you are the subject, the verb takes *-o* and is followed by *de*.

pitfalls.wrong: Yo sorprendo lo rápido que aprende.
pitfalls.right: Me sorprende lo rápido que aprende.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Without *me*, you are the one doing the surprising; for "it surprises me" the *me* has to come first.

pitfalls.wrong: Me sorprende de que esté vacía.
pitfalls.why: Almost. With *me sorprende* there is no *de*; *me sorprendo de que* has it.
Almost. The verb agrees with what causes the feeling, and *sus preguntas* is plural.

personal: Say one thing that surprises you and one moment when you felt sad or ashamed, using both patterns.
